summary: Lists the messages that CCN's NETRJS server may send to a remote user, covering the initial connection, sign-on and sign-off. The messages explain problems such as busy ports and what to do about them.

eli5.summary: When a user connects to a remote job service, it sometimes replies with error notes. This is the dictionary of what those notes mean.

questions: ccn remote job entry error messages
subtitle: A reference for error messages from the CCN remote job entry service

tldr.problem: When users submitted jobs remotely to the CCN (UCLA's Computer Communications Node) via the NETRJS protocol, they received error and status messages but had no reference for what the message codes meant.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 589 documents every message the CCN NETRJS server sends to remote users, organised by category: initial connection and sign-on, remote site or network failures, and CCN software failures. Each message is shown with its code and a plain-language explanation.
tldr.outcome: Users and system administrators had a complete reference for interpreting NETRJS messages and diagnosing connection, data transfer and software problems.

today: RFC 589 is a technical reference for the CCN NETRJS service, documenting its error messages and status codes. Remote job entry was a key way researchers used ARPANET in the early years. The CCN and its NETRJS service are long since retired, but this RFC is valuable for understanding how ARPANET's remote computing services worked and what problems administrators and users had to diagnose.

sections.title: NETRJS Server Messages
sections.content:
NETRJS is the protocol for submitting batch jobs to a remote computer over ARPANET. When a user connects to the CCN (UCLA's Computer Communications Node) and submits a job for remote execution, the server sends back messages about the outcome. This RFC catalogs all the messages the CCN NETRJS server sends to remote users.

The messages are organized into three categories: those during initial connection, sign-on and sign-off; those indicating remote site or network failures during data transfer; and those indicating problems with the CCN software itself.
sections.eli5: NETRJS is a way to send jobs to a distant computer. This RFC lists all the reply messages it can send and what they mean.

sections.title: Connection and Session Messages
sections.content: When a user initiates the ICP (Initial Connection Protocol) to a NETRJS socket, the CCN might refuse the connection if there is no free core memory in the NCP region or if CCN's software is crashing. If the connection succeeds, the server sends a READY message (NRJ876R CCN NETRJS READY. ENTER SIGNON). If the user sends no input for 3 minutes, the session times out with messages NRJ308R SIGNON TIMEOUT EXCEEDED and NRJ205R NETRJS SESSION TERMINATED. An invalid signon receives NRJ307R INVALID SIGNON, RE-ENTER. A successful signon is acknowledged by RJS750I TERMINAL -termid- HAS SIGNED ONTO RJS. When the user ends the session with a SIGNOFF command, the server waits for data transfer to complete and sends NRJ205R NETRJS SESSION TERMINATED before closing the connection.
sections.eli5: When you log in, the server says 'ready'. If you don't respond in 3 minutes, it gives up. Once you log in successfully, you get a welcome message.

sections.title: Data Transfer and Network Failures
sections.content: During file transfer, if the remote user is too slow to respond, CCN closes the connection after 5 minutes with code NRJ504I DATA TRANSFER TIMEOUT. The code indicates whether the timeout was on a READER (incoming data), PRINTER or PUNCH (outgoing data) stream. If data is corrupted due to transmission errors or local software bugs, messages like NRJ505I BAD HEADER SEQUENCE FOR NETRJS READER, NRJ506I BAD HEADER LENGTH, or NRJ507I BAD HEADER TYPE are sent. For individual corrupted data records (header correct but data bad), the server sends NRJ602I line STREAM ERROR - READER, -code- with codes 1-7 indicating specific problems such as truncated input or string overflow. If the user intentionally aborts, the message is NRJ502I NETRJS -device- DATA TRANSFER ABORTED BY USER -termid-.
sections.eli5: If the file transfer is too slow, the server waits 5 minutes then gives up. If the data gets scrambled, you get an error code saying what's wrong.

sections.title: CCN Software Failures
sections.content: Several classes of messages indicate serious problems with CCN's network software. The CCN operator can cancel a session entirely with NRJ204I NETRJS SESSION ABORTED BY CENTRAL OPERATOR, TERM=-termid-. Catastrophic software failures include NRJ106A NETRJS DEAD - EXCHANGE INOPERATIVE, NRJ201A NETRJS DT SOCKET ERROR - BAD LISTEN, NRJ208A NETRJS PROGRAM CHECK IN -device-, code=ccc, and several others. These messages all cause the session to abort immediately and should be reported to CCN. Additionally, a user might encounter a data transfer process failure that does not terminate the entire session, only the current data connection—messages like NRJ501I NO CORE FOR DATA TRANSFER BUFFER -device- or NRJ509I -device- DATA TRANSFER DEAD. These problems may be transient and can be retried, but repeated failures should be reported.
sections.eli5: Sometimes the CCN computer itself has serious problems. An operator can shut down your session. Or the file transfer process can crash but the connection survives.
